title: Phase 4: Cohesive module and class decomposition
status_detail: Inactive Phase 4; package-, module-, and contract-specific refactor children will be determined later from accepted inventory and public-boundary results.
objective: Decompose overloaded Python modules and classes into cohesive domain owners while preserving accepted behavior, contracts, dependency direction, and evidence meaning.
authorized_scope: After accepted prerequisite results and separate activation, create bounded descendants for independently refactorable package, module, serializer, repository, workflow, integration, or validation responsibilities.

Move intrinsic invariants to their DataObject or ResultObject, reusable policy and cross-object behavior to cohesive ActionObjects, wire mechanics to serializers, and genuine multi-step composition to Workflows without generic utility owners.

Split large files and classes according to contract and dependency cohesion, remove prohibited dangling behavior and private ownership under the accepted Phase 1 rule, and preserve deliberate supported imports through the Phase 3 boundary.
Migrate tests and documentation with each bounded refactor, retaining evidence meaning and requiring explicit decisions for material public, wire, numerical, or scientific changes.
completion_criteria: Every activated descendant has one cohesive responsibility, explicit dependencies, non-overlapping path ownership when required, and verification proportional to its affected contracts.
The accepted candidate register is fully dispositioned as refactored, retained with rationale, superseded, or explicitly deferred; line-count reduction alone is not treated as completion.
Affected source, tests, typing, documentation, imports, fixtures, schemas, and compatibility behavior agree without dangling callables, generic utility containers, or hidden cross-object policy.
Aggregate architecture conformance passes for all migrated modules, residual debt remains explicit, and no unselected descendant or successor is activated automatically.
exclusions: Do not perform one repository-wide mechanical move, blind rename, or compatibility facade expansion in place of bounded responsibility-driven refactors.
Do not weaken tests, tolerances, typing, documentation, schemas, or accepted public behavior merely to simplify a split.
Do not combine unrelated domain responsibilities, introduce speculative Rust structure, or alter scientific meaning or protected execution boundaries.
No dependency change, release, staging, commit, push, or automatic activation is authorized by this inactive Task.
